label: text
text: CHAIRMAN'S REFERENCE.

label: text
text: Hongkong Amusements Meeting Discussion.

label: text
text: The views of members of the public as to the price charged for cinema seats was referred to at the fifth ordinary yearly meeting of shareholders of the Hongkong Amusements, Ltd., when the Chairman, Mr. J. H. Backhouse, referring to the accounts, said that if two cents less per head had been charged for admission the working of the Company would have shown a net loss instead of a net earning.

label: text
text: As a result of discussion on the extraordinary resolution for the consolidation of shares and the proposing of an amendment to that resolution by Mr. Lo Kan, one of the managing directors, the meeting called with reference to the passing of this extraordinary resolution was postponed for a week.

label: text
text: Those present at the meeting, in addition to the Chairman, were: Messrs. H. W. Rays and Lo. Kan (managing directors); Lo Shunwan, J. M. Noronha, R. E. Ost and Ma Tsui-chiu (directors); also the following shareholders; Messrs. A. Nemazee, Wong Ping-sun, Lo Chung-kue, H. H. Priestley, J. T. Choy, F. Gonzales and others.

label: text
text: The Chairman's speech at the first meeting was as follows:

label: text
text: I formally move that the report and statement of accounts as presented, be received, approved and adopted. If my remarks last year were short, this year they will be shorter still.

label: text
text: I can afford to be so very brief because on this occasion there appear to be no explanation, necessary or desirable except perhaps in one or two directions. The year's work under review, viz., 1925-6, has seen a great increase in the scope of our business. Our plans, as briefly intimated to you at our annual meeting last year, have fractified, resulting in the acquisition of the Queen's and World Theatres during the year. The Queen's Theatre was taken over by your company from August 1, 1925, and the World Theatre was acquired from the Hongkong Government during the latter part of September, 1925, and to date, both theatres have been working very satisfactorily. Owing to the close proximity to the Queen's, the Coronet Theatre—our former popular 'Little House'—was closed on our taking over the Colony's premier cinema house.

label: paragraph_title
text: Boycott Effect

label: text
text: The boycott and crisis which commenced in June of last year has caused considerable anxiety in the commercial sphere of this Colony. The facts are too well known to all and it is needless for me to make any comment except perhaps in connection with the effect of our chain of theatres. The situation naturally hit our Chinese theatres very seriously, namely, the Grand Theatre at Wanchai, the New Taiyat Theatre at Yaumati and the Cheong Lok Theatre at Sai-wan-ho, which are situated in the heart of industrial and labouring districts. Fortunately, however, the effect did not continue for long and after a few months, conditions returned to a more or less normal state.

label: text
text: Owing to considerably increased expenditure and overhead consequent upon our taking over two of the Colony's largest theatres your directors regret that they are unable to repeat the previous year's dividend of 20 per cent. but they are recommending a dividend of 15 per cent. which, I feel sure, in view of the company's increased overhead and the troublous period through which we have all experienced, will be a source of gratification to you just as surely as it is to them, especially as we are able to carry forward an amount of some $26,000—representing nearly 60 per cent. above last year's figure. We have every reason to hope that the immediate future will yield even better results.

FINANCIAL SITUATION
NOT ALARMING

label: text
text: FOREIGN REPORTS DENIED.

label: text
text: The Canton Information Bureau has issued the following “communique through Reuter's Agency:—

label: paragraph_title
text: Canton, Aug. 9.

label: text
text: The postal workers resumed work this morning.

label: text
text: The reports appearing in foreign newspapers describing the financial situation here as alarming are entirely false.

label: text
text: The demonstration on Sunday against the resumption of the Peking Tariff Conference was attended by large crowds.

label: text
text: I would point out that approximately 21% million people visited all our theatres in a year and if we had charged 2 cents less per head for admission we would show a net loss of some $5,000—instead of a net earning of nearly $40,000—a fact which clearly indicates the very small margin on which your company is working.

label: text
text: As last year, we have budgeted for a bonus to be paid to Chinese theatre staffs, which will not exceed $960. You will, I am sure, cordially approve this recognition of faithful and arduous service.

label: text
text: I thank you, gentlemen, for the patient hearing you have given my remarks, and take pleasure in calling on Mr. J. M. Noronha to second the resolution now before you, viz., that the report and statement of accounts as presented, be received, approved and adopted.

label: paragraph_title
text: Other Business.

label: text
text: Mr. Noronha having seconded and there being no questions the report and accounts were unanimously adopted.

label: text
text: Mr. Ray proposed the re-election to the Board of Directors of Mr. J. M. Noronha and Mr. Ma Tsui-chiu and the election of Mr. J. Gubbay and on behalf of himself and Mr. Lo Kan thanked the directors for the assistance they had given during the past year which had been a difficult one. Mr. Backhouse, particularly, had given hours and hours of his time during that difficult period and other directors had been no less helpful in the devotion of their time and the making of helpful suggestions.

label: text
text: The directors proposed by Mr. Ray were elected unanimously, Mr. Lo Kan seconding.

label: text
text: The Chairman made a proposal with regard to payment of dividend in accordance with the declaration in his speech, Mr. Ost.

label: text
text: Mr. R. E. Lindsell and Major C. Willson sat together at the Central Magistracy this morning to deal with, the charge of unlawful possession of arms against a ship's painter of the s.s. "Fatshan" formally adjourned from Saturday.

label: text
text: The case was one in which an attempt was made to lower the arms which had been placed in floating containers when the ship was on the outward voyage between Capsuimum and Castle Peak. A "sampun" with a man's hat hoisted on a pole was to take possession of the arms as arranged by the smugglers. This sampun was, in fact, passed by the s.s. "Fatshan" after the discovery had been made by the ship's officers, also on the downward voyage, apparently still hopeful of the arms being lowered.

label: text
text: The arms taken over by Acting Inspector J. Moss, who had charge of the case, comprised 20 Mauser pistols, 42 Smith and Wesson revolvers, 40 magazines and 3,250 rounds of ammunition.

label: text
text: Defendant, who had stated to the police that the arms were given to him by a travelling trader to take to Canton, admitted the charge.

label: text
text: Mr. Lindsell: You were smuggling them to Canton?

kong yourself?

label: text
text:

label: text
text: Defendant, who appeared to contradict His Worship on this point, was sentenced to three years' hard labour, an order being made for the arms to be confiscated.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: Mystery surrounds the sinking of H29 within a few minutes.

label: text
text: The Commander-in-Chief has arrived. He took charge of the special equipment which was rushed to the quayside to raise the vessel.

label: text
text: The submarine had just returned from tests, the hatches being open and the propeller had not stopped. When she came alongside she suddenly tilted and sank within ninety seconds.

label: text

label: text
text: RESUMPTION DEPENDS ON NANKOW?

label: text
text: EFFECT OF THE WAR.

label: text
text: Interesting Intelligence From Canton.

label: text
text: Few foreign residents in the Colony pay much attention to the fortunes of war in North China and even the Chinese themselves are at a loss to make out the precise position but from an unofficial source it is learned that the fighting at Nankow has considerable influence on the prospects of the boycott conference being resumed.

label: text
text: The gist of the intelligence gathered by a correspondent is that the Canton authorities are waiting to come to a decision. Some days ago, the conference adjourned. The Hongkong deligation came back to await instructions and the Canton Government was to consider the proffered loan of $10,000,000 for development work.

label: paragraph_title
text: Where the Rivals Are

label: text
text: General Chang Kai-shek, commander-in-chief, is at "the southern China front while his civil officials are" mostly in Canton.

label: text
text:
Hunan is the province separating Kwangtung from the Yangtze Valley (central China). The Nationalist Front is reported to be near Changsha and Wu Pei-fu's troops are near Yochow, a town on the railway between Changsha and Hankow (the latter erstwhile the capital of Wu Pei-fu).
Operations on this front are partly restricted. It seems that Canton's forces are awaiting developments before making another advance. On the other hand, Wu Pei-fu's subordinates are marking time pending the return of their leader from the North.

label: text
text: Wu Pei-fu's Movements.

label: text
text: Marshal Wu has been quoted as having promised to return to Hankow so soon as the campaign in North China is concluded.

label: text
text: Further north than Peking, the army of Feng Yu-hsiang (the Christian general). known as the Kuominchun, are holding on to Nankow Pass, on the road to Kalgan, their main camp.

label: text
text: Vernacular cables report a continuous assault on Nankow and Reuter has stated that firing has been heard in Peking.

label: text
text: Should Nankow fall, then it is presumed that Wu Pei-fu will leave the North to Marshal Chang Tso-lin (warlord of Manchuria). The conclusion is that he will go back to central China where his presence will tend to a central command, and prestige—and possibly an extension of hostilities in Hunan, thereby engaging the attention of Canton.

label: paragraph_title
text: Canton Waiting?

label: text
text: The correspondent remarks that Canton is waiting to see how things will pan out at Nankow. Should the Kuominchun win then it is likely that the Nationalists will push forward and consolidate their position before re-opening the conference with Hongkong to end the boycott. Victory for Wu Pei-fu (and Chang Tso-lin) at Nankow will adversely affect Canton's prospects in Hunan and may hasten the resumption of the adjourned conference.

label: text
text: The consensus of opinion in Canton, from a well-informed source, is that the interval before resumption may not end just yet.
